Based in San Francisco, Arine is a rapidly growing healthcare technology and clinical services company with a mission to ensure individuals receive the safest and most effective treatments for their unique and evolving healthcare needs.
Frequently, medications cause more harm than good. Incorrect drugs and doses costs the US healthcare system over $528 billion in waste, avoidable harm, and hospitalizations each year. Arine is redefining what excellent healthcare looks like by solving these issues through our software platform (SaaS).

We combine cutting edge data science, machine learning, AI, and deep clinical expertise to introduce a patient-centric view to medication management, and develop and deliver personalized care plans on a massive scale for patients and their care teams.
Arine is committed to improving the lives and health of complex patients that have an outsized impact on healthcare costs and have traditionally been difficult to identify and address.

These patients face numerous challenges including complicated prescribing issues across multiple medications and providers, medication challenges with many chronic diseases, and patient issues with access to care.

Backed by leading healthcare investors and collaborating with top healthcare organizations and providers, we deliver recommendations and facilitate clinical interventions that lead to significant, measurable health improvements for patients and cost savings for customers.

s.h: Why is Arine a Great Place to Work?
s.t:
Outstanding Team and Culture - Our shared mission unites and motivates us to do our best work. We have a relentless passion and commitment to the innovation required to be the market leader in medication intelligence.
Making a Proven Difference in Healthcare - We are saving patient lives, and enabling individuals to experience improved health outcomes, including significant reductions in hospitalizations and cost of care.
Market Opportunity - Arine is backed by leading healthcare investors and was founded to tackle one of the largest healthcare problems today. Non-optimized medications therapies which cost the US 275,000 lives and $528 billion annually.
Dramatic Growth - Arine is managing more than 18 million lives across prominent health plans after only 4 years in the market, and was ranked 236 on the 2024 Inc. 5000 list and was named the 5th fastest-growing company in the AI category.

We are looking for a Clinical Program Pharmacist to join a strong team of clinicians, data scientists, and engineers to develop and maintain Arine’s software platform and to help optimize patient outcomes for our clients.

As a Clinical Program Pharmacist, you will be a part of building a product that helps clinicians provide expert level medication therapy consultation to patients and their providers.

You will collaborate closely with Engineering, Product, Implementation, Client Success, and Data Analyst teams to improve Arine’s software platform, and will be expected to supervise and maintain the clinical quality of our product content, as well as assist in clinical program development.

You will serve as a liaison for patients and outside providers on product enhancements as the platform expert, and have a direct impact on patient care through the delivery of our core enterprise by keeping continually abreast of new developments in the fast-moving drug field while being aware of emerging patterns, treatment guidelines, and best practices.

All team members foster cooperative working relationships with clients and colleagues by communicating effectively, being respectful, and accepting feedback professionally. Additionally, all members act to meet patient needs and learn new skills to achieve quality customer service and patient care.
The Clinical Program Pharmacist receives assignments and functions under the supervision of Clinical Program Pharmacist Leads as well as the VP of Clinical Programs to carry out and supervise direct patient care responsibilities and program development.

The essential functions listed are typical examples of work performed by positions in this job classification. They are not intended to be a comprehensive inventory of all duties, tasks, and responsibilities. Employees may also perform other duties as assigned.
The role encompasses all of Arine's Clinical Program team activities. Job duties also include review and evaluation of clinical guidelines, writing effective and compelling recommendations to different stakeholders, performing quality assurance on all customer deliverables, providing clinical expertise during implementation, training, and program development.

Improve clinical algorithms, workflows, and performance metrics based on new quality measures and clinical guidelines.
Communicate effectively in both written and oral formats to help interpret and resolve clinical issues or collaborate on new solutions with various stakeholders including but not limited to engineering, product, clinical care team, and clients
Develop intervention strategies to optimize medication utilization, achieve quality measures, and other established goals

Comply with all company policies and state and federal rules and regulations

The clinical pharmacist ensures, effective medication use by assessing therapy, dispensing accurately, monitoring outcomes, educating patients and staffing, and resolving medication issues. ii.

Conducts patient counseling before discharge (including patient/family education), fulfills medication reconciliation duties, and documents the encounter, following these steps: 1. Collect a complete list of current medications from the discharging service.

Compare the validated and updated list to the provider's discharge instructions and discharge medication orders. 4. Make recommendations about drug therapy by comparing the medication list with provider orders, taking into account the patient's medical condition and any refill needs. 5.

Document all collected and validated information in the patient's electronic medical chart. 6. Verify and prepare oncology medications safely , monitors, collaborate, and support care. 7. Provide consultation to physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals regarding drug therapy. 8.

Addresses consults related to herbal medications, non-VA medications, and renal dosing considerations. 12. Reviews new medication orders for duplication, allergies, and continuity of care. 13. Participates in Quality Assurance programs as directed by the supervisor. i.

Provides clinical pharmacy information and supports services to ensure optimal therapy. v. Works with outpatient pharmacy and staff to support seamless medication processes for discharging patients. Resolves drug distribution issues and supports quality assurance programs. C.

Formulary Management i. Participates in developing policies, procedures, criteria for use, and guidelines related to drug therapy. ii. Provides training, and orientation to pharmacy staff, students, and residents to support competency and professional development ii. Educates patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals on medication therapy, safe medication practices, and clinical pharmacy services. iii.

Provides medication-related information to patients and healthcare staff. iv. Delivers in-service education to pharmacists, residents, interns, students, nurses, medical students, and other healthcare professionals. v.
